paragraphs.title: Commitment to Praise and God's Greatness

easy.explanation: He says, “I will bless thy name,” addressing the LORD.
easy.q: Whom does the psalmist promise to bless?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “Every day will I bless thee.”
easy.q: How often does the psalmist say he will bless the LORD?
How is the LORD's greatness described?

medium.explanation: The phrase indicates praise without end.
medium.q: What does “for ever and ever” show about the psalmist's praise?

answers: I will exalt and praise thee
medium.explanation: To extol is to exalt or praise greatly.
medium.q: What does “I will extol thee” mean?

medium.explanation: The verse directly calls His greatness “unsearchable.”
medium.q: Why can God's greatness not be fully searched out?

challenge.explanation: Both verses express the psalmist's ongoing commitment to bless and praise the LORD.
challenge.q: What common idea appears in verses 1–2?

challenge.explanation: The LORD's unsearchable greatness gives reason for continual praise.
challenge.q: How does verse 3 explain the psalmist's commitment to praise?

challenge.explanation: The first phrase emphasizes duration, and the second emphasizes God's limitless greatness.
challenge.q: Which phrases emphasize both lasting praise and limitless greatness?

paragraphs.title: Praise Passed from Generation to Generation

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “One generation shall praise thy works to another.”
easy.q: Who praises God's works from one generation to another?

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says they “shall declare thy mighty acts.”
Verse 7 says they “shall sing of thy righteousness.”
easy.q: What do people sing about in verse 7?

medium.explanation: “Wondrous works” means remarkable or wonderful deeds.
The passage uses words such as “praise,” “declare,” “speak,” and “utter.”
medium.q: How is praise passed from generation to generation?

answers: From mighty acts to goodness and righteousness
medium.explanation: The passage moves from God's works and power to His goodness and righteousness.
medium.q: How do verses 4–7 develop their subject?

challenge.explanation: The phrase “one generation...to another” presents continual transmission.
challenge.q: What preserves the memory of God's works?

answers: Praise belongs only to the past
challenge.explanation: The verbs describe praise being communicated aloud.
challenge.q: What do the many speaking verbs in verses 4–7 suggest?

answers: Works, mighty acts, wonders, goodness, and righteousness
challenge.explanation: These are the successive themes in the passage's praise.

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “The LORD is gracious, and full of compassion.”
easy.q: How is the LORD described in verse 8?

easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “his tender mercies are over all his works.”
easy.q: Over whom are God's tender mercies?

easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “All thy works shall praise thee.”
easy.q: Who praises the LORD in verse 10?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes patience and restraint.

answers: His goodness and mercy extend over them
medium.explanation: Verse 9 emphasizes that His tender mercies are over all His works.
medium.q: Why do all God's works praise Him in this passage?

medium.explanation: Verse 10 says, “his saints shall bless thee.”
medium.q: What do God's saints do in addition to the praise of all His works?

answers: All works praise, and saints bless
challenge.explanation: The verse separately mentions all God's works and His saints.

answers: His mercy leads to praise and blessing
His distance leads only to fear
challenge.explanation: His grace, compassion, patience, and mercy provide reason for praise.
challenge.q: How do God's qualities in verse 8 relate to the response in verse 10?

answers: The broad extent of mercy and praise
challenge.explanation: “All his works” and “all thy works” stress the universal scope of God's goodness and praise.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by “all” in verses 9–10?

paragraphs.title: The Glory and Permanence of God's Kingdom

answers: The glory of God's kingdom and His power
easy.explanation: Verse 11 mentions “the glory of thy kingdom” and “thy power.”
easy.q: What do people speak about in verse 11?

easy.explanation: Verse 12 says they are made known “to the sons of men.”
easy.q: To whom are God's mighty acts and kingdom made known?

answers: Those who fall and those bowed down
easy.explanation: Verse 14 says He upholds those who fall and raises those bowed down.
easy.q: Whom does the LORD uphold and raise up?

medium.explanation: To raise up is to lift or restore someone who is bowed down.
medium.q: What does “raiseth up” mean in verse 14?

answers: Speaking of the kingdom makes its power known
medium.explanation: The kingdom's glory and power are proclaimed so people may know them.

medium.q: How long does God's kingdom endure?

challenge.explanation: The passage combines glory and power with everlasting rule through all generations.
challenge.q: Which combination best describes God's kingdom in verses 11–13?

answers: God supports and lifts the weak
challenge.explanation: Both verbs describe God's help for those who fall or are bowed down.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the words “upholdeth” and “raiseth up”?

answers: The eternal King actively helps the needy
challenge.explanation: The passage presents God's enduring rule as a rule that supports and raises the vulnerable.
challenge.q: How does verse 14 complement the everlasting kingdom in verse 13?

easy.explanation: Verse 15 says, “The eyes of all wait upon thee.”
easy.q: To whom do all eyes wait in verse 15?

easy.explanation: Verse 15 says, “thou givest them their meat in due season.”
easy.q: What does God give living creatures in due season?

answers: Those who call upon Him in truth
easy.explanation: Verse 18 says He is near to all who call upon Him in truth.
easy.q: To whom is the LORD nigh?

answers: Look to and depend on thee
medium.explanation: The phrase describes looking to God with expectation and dependence.
medium.q: What does “wait upon thee” mean in verse 15?

answers: He satisfies the desire of every living thing
medium.explanation: Verse 16 says He satisfies the desire of every living thing.
medium.q: What happens when God opens His hand?

answers: He hears their cry and saves them
medium.explanation: Verse 19 says He hears their cry and saves them.
medium.q: What does God do for those who fear Him?

answers: All wait, God gives, and God satisfies
All are silent, God hides, and they fall
All flee, God withdraws, and they hunger
challenge.explanation: The verses show creation depending on God and receiving provision from Him.

answers: He hears and saves the fearful, and preserves those who love Him
challenge.explanation: Verse 19 emphasizes hearing and saving; verse 20 emphasizes preserving.
challenge.q: What is the difference between God's treatment of those who fear Him and those who love Him?

answers: All flesh is called to bless God's holy name
The psalm asks only for food
challenge.explanation: Verse 21 ends with a call for all flesh to bless God's holy name forever.
